reviews.comment: One of the strangest classes I've ever taken. He's interesting when lecturing, but mostly he asks questions and has you Google the answers. He cancels about half the classes. He doesn't use Canvas, so there's no way to check how you're doing. The class is not difficult per se, but your effort doesn't really have a connection to the grade you get.

He cancels class a lot. The topic we had was Immigration. It was pretty eye-opening, and reading theorists like Huntington was also different. But he's very unprofessional when grading and releasing grades. He doesn't post them and is pretty irresponsible. I feel like he picks grades out of a hat.

Mr. Vacano is overall a good professor. His lectures are good but sometimes tough to take notes on. Multiple extra credit opportunities are offered. Make sure to participate in debates and discussion. Also keep up with the readings! He does not enter grades manually on Canvas so it's not always clear what grade you have.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don't listen to the negative reviews. While it's frustrating that heh doesn't enter grades into Canvas, the class is SO worth it. The lectures are so interesting and he is passionate about what he does. If you go to class you will make an A... it's that simple. There's little to no homework, you just have to read a little bit before most classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Vocano's course is the most dysfunctional course I have taken during my time at TAMU. Does not utilize Canvas so there is no transparency regarding grades. He was not only bad at communication but scrutinized students for asking questions and even attacked my own academic abilities without taking the time to understand my personal circumstances.

This prof was brilliant and his course was chill. Even though, I did not need it, there was extra credit available, and that was reassuring. If only I had taken more classes with him because I learned a TON on the history/political theory of the Americas. If you have any questions just go see him during office hours. He is funny and easy going.

Professor Von Vacano is a very good professor and is very passionate about his work. The class is graded by very few assignments, but Von Vacano tells you exactly what you need to do to get an A. This semester he offered a lot of extra credit for any student who wanted them. Be ready to read as we were assigned some pretty lengthy readings.

Look if you want a class that is super organized with clear criteria and ample feedback, then do no take this professor. If you want a class that is going to make you think, that's going to be intellectually challenging, and that will actually make you learn things (without being an overly difficult A), you won't find a better course.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class itself and the professor isnt bad, its just thoroughly unorganized and disorienting. The professor doesnt enter any grades, so you dont know your grade is until after the final essay. The professor also tends to assign random assignments that only have a vague corolation with the class itself.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His grading criteria is vague when he assigns things, then specific when he grades them. He loves to not teach something and then get made at students for not knowing it. His lectures are fine, but he just puts no effort into the class. Thin skinned and prone to anger. When students skip or miss assignments, he takes it out on the whole class.

Doctor Von Vacano is very passionate about Latin American philosophy. His lectures are very interesting and from time to time he cracks hilarious jokes. The one problem is his grading scale. Participation is a major part and the two essays. However, you wont know your grade until the last moment, no mid-term grade, etc. Little feedback.

Very unclear requirements for papers. Basis your final grade on literally 2 papers, despite the fact that you will be assigned a presentation as well as weekly memos. Successful grades on the project and memos are completely irrelevant, as the papers and his personal opinion will determine your grade. Also, its very difficult to ask him questions.

Dr. von Vacano's class is interesting. The class wasn't organized very well, and it was mainly discussion-based lectures with in-class debates here and there. Grades consist of 2 papers, weekly memos, a class presentation, and pop quizzes. His class was actually enjoyable and not very stressful; just make sure to participate, he's big on that.
took his Latin American Political Thought and Immigration ethics class, both excellent
